title: The Three Marks
question: Buddhist teaching marks all conditioned things with three characteristics. Joined with suffering and non-self, what completes the trio?
correctExplanation: Universal impermanence (anicca) — all compounded things dissolve: bodies, thoughts, nations. Three marks describe, never condemn.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is universal impermanence. Permanence, creation, and souls miss it: anicca joins dukkha and anatta as existence's fine print. Marks describe reality's terms, not its flaws.
lessonContent:
Fine print precedes all signatures.
Compounds dissolve by definition here.
Marks describe; they never condemn.
Three characteristics frame everything made.
Share this: watch one compound dissolve.

title: The Clinging Cause
question: The second noble truth locates suffering's origin not in pain itself but in our stance toward experience. What causes suffering?
correctExplanation: Clinging and craving (upādāna, taṇhā) — grasping at pleasant, shoving away unpleasant. Pain happens; suffering is the grip.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is clinging and craving. Events, luck, and others miss it: pain arrives uninvited, suffering checks in by choice. Grip, not circumstance, manufactures misery.
lessonContent:
Grips manufacture miseries reliably.
Pain arrives; suffering checks in chosen.
Stances cause more than events do.
Craving grasps; aversion shoves.
Share this: ungrip one held thing.

title: The Reverse Grip
question: Clinging pulls pleasant things close — but pushing unpleasant things away with equal force is also bondage. What is aversion?
correctExplanation: Clinging in reverse — aversion grips by pushing: hatred binds as tightly as hunger. Both directions shackle.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is clinging in reverse. Wisdom, boundaries, and courage miss it: shoving hardens contact exactly like grasping. Pushers stay as bound as pullers.
lessonContent:
Pushing hardens contact like grasping.
Shovers stay bound as pullers do.
Hatred grips with both hands too.
Reverse gears drive same bondage.
Share this: unpush one shoved thing.

title: The Unbinding
question: Nirvana is routinely mistaken for a Buddhist heaven of eternal bliss. Literally 'blowing out,' what does the word actually name?
correctExplanation: Cessation of clinging — greed, hatred, delusion blown out like flames. Cooling, not crowning: the end of fuel.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is cessation of clinging fires. Paradises, reunions, and youth miss it: nirvana extinguishes, never enthrones. Blowing out ends burning.
lessonContent:
Extinguishing ends burning completely.
Cooling, never crowning, defines peace.
Fires out mean suffering unfueled.
Blowing out beats building up.
Share this: blow out one small fire.

title: The Mustard Search
question: Grief-mad Kisa Gotami was told to fetch mustard seed from a house untouched by death. What did the impossible errand teach?
correctExplanation: Universality of loss — every door had mourned: her private grief joined the human commons. Errands teach what sermons cannot.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is universality of loss. Farming, storage, and maps miss it: door after door confessed dead. Private agonies dissolve into shared condition.
lessonContent:
Shared conditions dissolve private agonies.
Every door confesses dead eventually.
Errands teach what sermons cannot.
Commons comfort better than counsel.
Share this: knock one mourning door.

title: The Abandoned Raft
question: The Buddha compared teachings to a raft: essential for crossing, absurd to carry afterward. What should happen to doctrines post-crossing?
correctExplanation: Abandonment after use — rafts serve rivers, not backs: clinging to teachings repeats the disease. Use fully, then set down.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is abandonment after use. Enshrinement, worship, and burial miss it: vehicles serve transits, never destinations. Carrying rafts ashore looks devout and walks slowly.
lessonContent:
Vehicles serve transits, never destinations.
Set down what carried you over.
Clinging to cures repeats diseases.
Use fully, then abandon freely.
Share this: beach one raft today.

title: The Second Arrow
question: Being struck hurts; raging at the strike — 'why me,' revenge fantasies — hurts separately. The Buddha distinguished two arrows. Which one is optional?
correctExplanation: The second arrow — pain arrives uninvited; suffering-about-pain is self-inflicted archery. First arrows wound; second arrows are volunteered.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the second arrow of reactivity. First arrows (pain) strike all bodies; second arrows (rage, pity, revenge) strike only volunteers. Archers of self wound selves most.
lessonContent:
Volunteers wound themselves secondarily.
Pain arrives; suffering enlists optionally.
Archery self-inflicted hurts worst.
First arrows wound all bodies.
Share this: dodge one second arrow.

title: The Heap Inquiry
question: Form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness — dissected one by one, no owner appears. What are these five?
correctExplanation: Five heaps (khandhas) — every experience decomposes into ownerless piles. Selves hide in none of them.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is five heaps. Senses, elements, and precepts miss it: form through consciousness exhaust experience without producing proprietors. Heaps, never holders, constitute persons.
lessonContent:
Heaps constitute persons, never holders.
Dissection finds piles, never owners.
Experience exhausts into ownerless piles.
Proprietors hide in no pile.
Share this: dissect one experience tonight.

title: The Ownerless House
question: Searching body and mind for an unchanging essence finds processes but no proprietor. What does this absence establish?
correctExplanation: No fixed self (anatta) — absence of essence, not of persons: selves function without foundations. Houses stand ownerless, fully furnished.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no fixed self. Nihilism, denial, and mechanism miss it: persons operate ownerlessly, like corporations act without ghost-CEOs. Function needs no essence.
lessonContent:
Function needs no essence ever.
Houses stand ownerless, furnished fully.
Persons operate without proprietors.
Absence liberates; it never negates.
Share this: inhabit one ownerless house.

title: The Missing Chariot
question: Nagasena asked King Milinda: point to the 'chariot' among wheels, axle, yoke, reins — nowhere found, yet kings ride. What does the analogy prove?
correctExplanation: No fixed self beyond parts — chariot names an arrangement, not an extra entity. Persons likewise: patterns, never proprietors.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no fixed self beyond parts. Nonexistence, riding bans, and illusions miss it: chariots function perfectly unowned. Arrangements suffice; essences add nothing.
lessonContent:
Arrangements suffice; essences add nothing.
Patterns function perfectly unowned.
Names label systems, never substances.
Chariots carry kingless kings daily.
Share this: disassemble one chariot mentally.

title: The Charnel School
question: Monks meditate in charnel grounds on bloating, discoloring, devoured bodies. What does this grim curriculum teach?
correctExplanation: Impermanence of the body — charnel facts internalized: this flesh futures likewise. Corpses instruct the living directly.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is impermanence of the body. Anatomy, darkness, and burials miss it: grounds teach owners their own trajectory. Future corpses meditate present ones.
lessonContent:
Grounds teach owners their trajectories.
Future corpses instruct present ones.
Flesh futures likewise, always.
Grim schools graduate undeluded minds.
Share this: visit one charnel thought.

title: The Daily Dying
question: Daily mindfulness of death is prescribed not to sadden practitioners but to energize them. What does death-awareness produce?
correctExplanation: Diligence in practice — maranasati converts mortality into urgency: days finite, practice now. Death meditated motivates.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is diligence in practice. Depression, police, and fear miss it: remembrance fuels rather than freezes. Finite days demand infinite care.
lessonContent:
Remembrance fuels rather than freezes.
Finite days demand infinite care.
Mortality meditated motivates fully.
Death aware, practice blazes.
Share this: die daily for diligence.

title: The Steady Scale
question: The sage meets praise and blame, gain and loss, with perfectly balanced mind. What virtue holds steady amid all eight winds?
correctExplanation: Balanced mind (upekkha) — steady amid winds, neither grasping gusts nor fleeing gales. Steadiness, not numbness.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is balanced mind. Indifference, suppression, and cynicism miss it: balance feels fully while clinging to nothing. Scales steady, winds blow on.
lessonContent:
Balance feels fully, clings never.
Scales steady while winds blow on.
Steadiness differs from numbness deeply.
Gusts pass; balances remain.
Share this: balance one wind today.

title: The Eight Winds
question: Gain and loss, fame and disrepute, praise and blame, pleasure and pain — the forces tossing worldlings about. How are they grouped?
correctExplanation: Eight worldly winds — four pairs tossing the unanchored: fortune's weather system mapped completely. Sages build shelters, not sails.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is eight worldly winds. Truths, poisons, and links miss it: gain-loss, fame-shame, praise-blame, pleasure-pain — eight gusts, one forecast. Weather mapped can be withstood.
lessonContent:
Weather mapped can be withstood.
Eight gusts, one forecast complete.
Shelters beat sails in storms.
Fortune's system mapped fully here.
Share this: shelter one gust today.

title: The Visiting Anger
question: Anger arrives, stays a while, and departs — observed mindfully, never obeyed. In this practice, what are emotions?
correctExplanation: Passing visitors — emotions transit consciousness without constituting it. Hosts need not become guests.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is passing visitors. Essences, messages, and errors miss it: anger visits, never moves in — unless obeyed. Observation hosts without identifying.
lessonContent:
Hosts need not become guests ever.
Visits end; identifications persist wrongly.
Observation hosts without merging.
Transients pass; awareness remains.
Share this: host one anger briefly.

title: The Begging Bowl
question: Monks beg daily food instead of storing wealth or earning wages. What does the bowl systematically teach?
correctExplanation: Dependence and humility — daily receiving dissolves self-sufficiency myths. Bowls teach interdependence bite by bite.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is dependence and humility. Cuisine, property, and recipes miss it: begging practices neediness openly. Self-sufficiency starves where bowls fill.
lessonContent:
Neediness openly practiced humbles deeply.
Bowls fill where self-sufficiency starves.
Receiving teaches what earning hides.
Interdependence bites daily here.
Share this: receive one gift openly.

title: The Centered Way
question: The Buddha tried sensual indulgence, then years of self-starvation; awakening came through neither extreme. What resulted?
correctExplanation: Middle path — between indulgence and mortification: nourished body, trained mind. Extremes fail symmetrically.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is middle path. Hedonism, withdrawal, and contests miss it: palace and forest both failed before the middle succeeded. Extremes teach by failing.
lessonContent:
Extremes teach by failing symmetrically.
Palace and forest both failed first.
Nourished bodies train minds best.
Middles succeed where edges starve.
Share this: walk one middle today.

title: The Starved Sage
question: Emaciated nearly to death by austerities, the future Buddha abandoned extreme fasting as fruitless. What did the failure teach?
correctExplanation: Extremes fail both ways — indulgence scatters, mortification weakens: only the middle sustains inquiry. Starvation taught by failing.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is extremes fail both ways. Meat, effortlessness, and sleep miss it: the skeleton proved asceticism bankrupt. Failure instructed where success misleads.
lessonContent:
Skeletons prove methods bankrupt truly.
Bankruptcy instructs better than success.
Indulgence scatters; mortification weakens.
Middles sustain what edges starve.
Share this: abandon one extreme.

title: The Kalamas' Charter
question: The Kalamas were told not to believe reports, traditions, or teachers — but to test teachings in their own experience. What authority remains standing?
correctExplanation: One's own testing — ehipassiko, come-and-see: verification by living, never by lineage. Experience outranks eminence.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is one's own testing. Loudness, royalty, and antiquity miss it: the charter democratizes verification radically. Test in living, not in libraries.
lessonContent:
Living verifies what lineage cannot.
Experience outranks eminence always.
Democratized verification empowers all.
Test teachings the way tasters taste.
Share this: test one teaching livedly.

title: The Final Instruction
question: 'Work out your salvation with diligence' ranks among the Buddha's attributed last words. Whose effort liberates?
correctExplanation: One's own effort — no savior outsources liberation: diligence is the whole vehicle. Last words assign first responsibility.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is one's own effort. Rituals, fees, and graces miss it: salvation un-outsourceable defines the teaching. Vehicles carry only willing walkers.
lessonContent:
Vehicles carry willing walkers only.
Liberation un-outsourceable defines paths.
Diligence is the whole vehicle.
Last words assign first responsibility.
Share this: walk diligently once.

title: The Watched Flame
question: Anger watched mindfully without being acted out tends to do what?
correctExplanation: Dissolve unacted — observed anger burns its fuel without finding targets. Watching metabolizes what indulgence feeds.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is dissolve unacted. Growth, possession, and permanence miss it: unwatched anger acts out, watched anger burns out. Attention digests what reaction feeds.
lessonContent:
Attention digests what reaction feeds.
Unwatched anger acts out fully.
Observed flames burn fuel only.
Watching metabolizes all fires.
Share this: watch one flame out.

title: The Nine Stages
question: Why contemplate corpses through nine stages of decay rather than meditate on beautiful bodies?
correctExplanation: To internalize impermanence — decay viewed directly rewires denial structurally. Beauty meditated flatters; corpses instruct.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is to internalize impermanence. Entertainment, medicine, and art miss it: nine stages leave denial nowhere to stand. Direct seeing beats beautiful thinking.
lessonContent:
Denial stands nowhere against corpses.
Direct seeing beats beautiful thinking.
Nine stages exhaust all euphemism.
Decay instructs the living precisely.
Share this: view one stage bravely.

title: The Triple Refuge
question: Amid universal flux, Buddhists take refuge in Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. What are these three?
correctExplanation: Refuges in change — teacher, teaching, community: reliable amid flux, not escapes from it. Shelter, not exemption.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is refuges in change. Gods, spells, and numbers miss it: refuge means reliable orientation, never immunity. Storms continue; sailors hold ropes.
lessonContent:
Orientation steadies amid storms fully.
Reliable differs from exempting always.
Ropes hold sailors, never calm seas.
Refuges guide; they never extract.
Share this: hold one rope steady.

title: The Warm Release
question: Critics call non-attachment cold indifference. Practitioners reply it frees a warmer response than clinging allowed. What survives clinging's end?
correctExplanation: Compassion freed — ungrasping love flows wider than needy love. Release warms what grip chilled.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is compassion freed. Apathy, numbness, and cynicism miss it: non-attachment removes grasping, never caring. Freed hands hold more gently.
lessonContent:
Ungrasping love flows wider always.
Release warms what gripping chilled.
Freed hands hold most gently.
Caring survives clinging's end fully.
Share this: free one caring today.

title: The Cloud Paper
question: Thich Nhat Hanh's interbeing: this sheet holds cloud, rain, logger, sunshine — nothing exists alone. What does everything do?
correctExplanation: Mutually arise — interbeing: all things co-originate, none self-sufficient. Paper contains weather systems.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is mutually arise. Separation, competition, and solitude miss it: remove cloud and paper vanishes. Co-arising describes reality's weave.
lessonContent:
Remove cloud and paper vanishes.
Co-arising weaves reality fully.
Nothing self-sufficient exists anywhere.
Sheets hold weather systems truly.
Share this: interbe with one sheet.
